questions.q: A man using exogenous testosterone has a normal serum testosterone concentration but suppressed LH and low intratesticular testosterone. Which process is most directly compromised?
options: Secretion of inhibin by Sertoli cells only
questions.explain: Exogenous testosterone suppresses hypothalamic GnRH and pituitary LH by negative feedback. Reduced LH stimulation of Leydig cells lowers intratesticular testosterone, which is required at high local concentrations for normal spermatogenesis. A normal serum testosterone concentration does not guarantee adequate intratesticular testosterone.

questions.q: Which pituitary hormone acts directly on Leydig cells to stimulate testosterone synthesis?
questions.explain: Luteinising hormone (LH) stimulates Leydig cells to synthesise testosterone. FSH acts mainly on Sertoli cells, supporting spermatogenesis and stimulating inhibin B production.

questions.q: Which cell is produced when a primary spermatocyte completes the first meiotic division?
questions.explain: Meiosis I divides a primary spermatocyte into two haploid secondary spermatocytes. Meiosis II then produces spermatids, which differentiate during spermiogenesis.

questions.q: Which autonomic pathway is chiefly responsible for initiating penile erection through nitric-oxide-mediated relaxation of cavernosal smooth muscle?
questions.explain: Parasympathetic outflow from S2–S4 promotes nitric oxide release and relaxation of cavernosal smooth muscle, increasing penile blood flow.

questions.q: Which autonomic division is chiefly responsible for emission of semen into the posterior urethra?
questions.explain: Emission is primarily sympathetic, involving contraction of the vas deferens, seminal vesicles and prostate with closure of the bladder neck. Expulsion also involves rhythmic somatic pelvic-floor contractions.
